explanation.markdown:
## Defining vs non-defining: Grammar chart

![Defining and non-defining relative clauses](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-1.png)

## Defining relative clauses

Defining relative clauses carry **essential information** because they **identify which** thing or person we are talking about, and they are used **without commas**.

-   *This is the music **which was used at the show**.* 
-   *Have they found the prisoner **who escaped last week**?*

#### We can use **that**

In defining relative clauses, we can use **that** instead of **which** or **who**.

-   *This is the music **that** was used at the show.* 
-   *Have they found the prisoner **that** escaped last week?*

#### When can we omit **who/which/that**?

**Who/which/that** can be **omitted** if they are followed by **subject + verb**

-   *Can you pass me the box **(which/that)** I keep in the top drawer?*
-   *You are not the man **(who/that)** I thought you were.* 

## Non-defining relative clauses

Non-defining relative clauses are used **between commas**, and they add **extra information**, which is **not necessary** to know who or what we are talking about.

-   *This music, **which I really like**, was used at the show.*
-   *My sister, **who I truly admire**, is coming for Thanksgiving.* 

#### We cannot use **that**, and we cannot omit **who/which**

In non-defining relative clauses (between commas), we cannot use **that**, and we cannot omit **who/which**.

-   *This music, **that I really like**, was used at the show.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-2.png)
-   *This music, **which I** **really** **like**, was used at the show.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-3.png)
-   *My sister, **I truly admire**, is coming for Thanksgiving.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-4.png)
-   *My sister, **whom I truly admire**, is coming for Thanksgiving.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-5.png)

## Defining vs non-defining relative clauses

In a defining relative clause, the information is essential to identify who or what we are talking about, whereas in non-defining relative clauses, we just add extra information, which is not necessary. Compare:

-   *My brother **who lives in Cardiff** is much older than me.* (=I have more than one brother, and the relative clause helps identify which brother I am talking about)
-   *My brother, **who lives in Cardiff**, is much older than me.* (=I have only one brother, so we don’t need the relative clause to know who I am talking about)

## Relative pronouns and adverbs

Here, you can see a grammar chart with the relative pronouns and adverbs that we normally use in relative clauses.  
  
![Relative clauses - Relative pronouns and relative adverbs](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-6.png)

## Common mistakes

#### Two subjects

When **who**, **which**, or **that** is the subject of a relative clause, we don’t use another pronoun or noun after it because we can only have one subject (**who**, **which**, or **that**). We can never have [two subjects in a sentence](https://test-english.com/grammar-points/shorts/how-to-avoid-double-subjects-in-english-grammar-shorts/).

-   *I saw a man **who he was** very tall.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-7.png)
-   *I saw a man **who was** very tall.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-8.png)
-   *That is the painting **that it was** stolen from the gallery.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-9.png)
-   *That is the painting **that was** stolen from the gallery.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-10.png)

#### **That** between commas

We cannot use the relative pronoun **that** in a non-defining relative clause (between commas)

-   *The victim, **that** suffered a concussion, said he didn’t remember the accident.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-11.png)
-   *The victim, **who** suffered a concussion, said he didn’t remember the accident.* ![](/uploads/grammar/b1/defining-and-non-defining-relative-clauses/img-12.png)
